title: 2016 AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: Jerry starts at \(0\) on the real number line. He tosses a fair coin \(8\) times. When he gets heads, he moves \(1\) unit in the positive direction; when he gets tails, he moves \(1\) unit in the negative direction. The probability that he reaches \(4\) at some time during this process is \(\dfrac{a}{b},\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(a+b?\) (For example, he succeeds if his sequence of tosses is HTHHHHHH.)

solutions.text:
Count the sequences of \(8\) tosses whose running total reaches \(4.\) With at most \(2\) tails he certainly reaches \(4,\) contributing \[ \begin{gathered} \binom80+\binom81+\binom82\\ =1+8+28\\ =37 \end{gathered} \] sequences.

With exactly \(3\) tails, he can first reach \(4\) on toss \(4\) or toss \(6.\) Reaching it on toss \(4\) requires four initial heads, after which the remaining head has \(4\) possible positions. Otherwise, tosses \(5\) and \(6\) are heads, one of the first four tosses is a tail, and the last two are tails, again giving \(4\) possibilities. Thus this case contributes \(8.\) With exactly \(4\) tails, only HHHHTTTT works, giving \(1.\) He cannot reach \(4\) with fewer than \(4\) heads.

So there are \(37+8+1=46\) favorable sequences out of \(2^8=256,\) a probability of \(\dfrac{46}{256}=\dfrac{23}{128}.\) Then \(a+b=23+128=151.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Count the \(2^8\) toss sequences in which the running total reaches \(4\)
With at most \(2\) tails he always reaches \(4;\) with \(3\) or \(4\) tails only some orders work
